name: News Corporation

profile.description: News Corporation is a global diversified media and information services company operating through five segments: Dow Jones (Wall Street Journal, Barron's, MarketWatch, Factiva), Digital Real Estate Services (REA Group, Move/Realtor.com), Book Publishing (HarperCollins), News Media (NY Post, The Times UK, The Australian), and subscription video services. FY2026 revenue reached $9.03B (+7% YoY) with net income of $743M (+15%) and 61% of revenues now digital. Controlled by the Murdoch family through dual-class share structure. Market cap approximately $17.4B.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): News Corp has executed a meaningful digital transformation over the past 5 years, shifting from a print-first media company to 61% digital revenue in FY2026 [1]. Dow Jones achieved a 30% profit margin through digital subscription growth and professional information services [2]. REA Group has become the dominant digital real estate platform in Australia with expanding international operations. HarperCollins pivoted to capitalize on digital and audio book formats. These represent a significant business model evolution across multiple segments. AI Deployment (1/2): News Corp has entered into AI content licensing agreements with major technology platforms, monetizing its proprietary content library for AI training purposes. CEO Robert Thomson positioned the company as proactive on AI, stating News Corp succeeded 'while other media companies have floundered' during the AI transition [3]. However, no specific AI-powered products shipping to customers or quantified internal savings were reported. Market Share (2/2): News Corp holds category leadership across multiple segments — The Wall Street Journal is the leading business newspaper in the U.S. by paid subscriptions, REA Group dominates Australian digital real estate with 95%+ market share, and HarperCollins is one of the Big Five global book publishers [1][2]. Product Pipeline (1/2): AI content licensing deals provide a new revenue stream, and digital real estate expansion (REA Group international growth, Move/Realtor.com) offers pipeline visibility, but no specific next-gen products with named launch dates were identified [1]. R&D Intensity (0/1): Technology spending appears at or near industry average for diversified media companies. No evidence of above-average R&D investment relative to peers.

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): News Corp articulates a purpose around creating and distributing authoritative and engaging content — a clear description of what the company does that connects journalism to an information-serving function for society [4]. The Wall Street Journal brand carries genuine weight as a public trust institution. However, the purpose does not articulate a transformative vision and is not distinctively different from other media companies. Community Impact (0/2): No distinctive community investment programs identified beyond standard corporate practices. News Corp's stated commitment to protecting the environment and contributing to communities appears in SEC filings but lacks specific programs or dollar amounts [4]. Employee Retention (0/2): Glassdoor reviews (1,011 reviews) describe a mixed culture. Some employees cite 'toxic' culture and poor management, while others note a 3.7/5.0 culture and values score and 4.0/5.0 for diversity and inclusion [3]. No specific retention or tenure data available. The dual-class share structure and Murdoch family control creates a governance dynamic that limits employee voice. Insider Buying (0/2): The Murdoch family controls News Corp through dual-class shares (Class B super-voting shares), which represents control alignment but not economic buying. No evidence of meaningful net insider purchases by executives in the last 12 months.

infrastructure.label: DEVELOPING
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on available metrics. News Corp's balance sheet is conservatively financed with D/E of 31.56%, well below the 70% target [5]. Revenue growth YoY of 10.8% exceeds the 10% target, driven by 11% Q4 growth and strength across all segments [1]. Forward P/E of 21.42x is slightly above the 20x target. However, the primary drags are low profitability and elevated valuation multiples relative to growth: profit margin of 6.35% is well below the 20% target, reflecting the capital-intensive media operations and legacy print costs. ROE of 7.98% is below the 15% target. The PEG ratio of 2.95 is near the 3.0 floor, reflecting the market's view that the current growth rate does not justify the valuation. Estimated 5-year revenue CAGR of ~3% reflects the structural challenges in traditional media, offset by digital growth. The stock clears the liquidity floor with ~$43.2M in daily trading volume.

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (5/9): News Corp's business faces mixed AI exposure across its segments. The News Media segment (NY Post, The Times UK, The Australian) is most exposed — AI can generate news summaries, reduce search referral traffic, and commoditize general news content, threatening advertising and subscription revenue [3]. Dow Jones faces AI pressure on its data and analytics products (Factiva, MarketWatch) as AI tools replicate research and summarization capabilities. However, the premium brand of The Wall Street Journal, proprietary financial data (OPIS, CMA), and original investigative journalism provide meaningful moats. Digital Real Estate Services (REA Group) is more defensible — property listings, lead generation, and local market expertise create switching costs that AI cannot easily replicate. Book Publishing (HarperCollins) faces emerging AI-authored content competition but benefits from author relationships, editorial curation, and distribution infrastructure. CEO Thomson has positioned News Corp proactively, entering AI content licensing deals that monetize the threat rather than merely absorbing it [3]. AI Opportunity (1/1): News Corp generates meaningful revenue from AI content licensing agreements with major technology platforms, monetizing its vast content archive for AI model training. These licensing deals represent a new revenue stream directly attributable to AI demand [1].

infinite_game.summary: News Corp under Murdoch family control is fundamentally a finite-game player — the company optimizes for media influence, financial returns, and competitive positioning rather than a Just Cause. While the digital transformation from print to 61% digital revenue demonstrates strategic adaptability, and CEO Thomson has navigated the AI disruption better than most media peers, the dual-class governance structure concentrating power in one family, mixed employee culture reviews, and competitive language focused on rivals' failures suggest a company playing to win rather than playing to endure.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): News Corp's stated purpose around creating and distributing authoritative content is a legitimate function but reads as a business description rather than a Just Cause [4]. The Wall Street Journal carries genuine institutional weight as a public trust, and the company's journalism does serve the democratic function of informing the public. However, under Murdoch family control, the company's strategic decisions are primarily driven by competitive positioning and financial returns rather than an articulated vision of a better future. The company has not demonstrated willingness to sacrifice commercial interest in service of its journalism mission.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): Glassdoor reviews describe a mixed-to-negative culture with terms like 'toxic' appearing alongside more positive reviews [3]. The dual-class share structure concentrating voting power in the Murdoch family creates a governance hierarchy that limits organizational voice and empowerment. The 2024 proxy fight over Murdoch family succession created public uncertainty about the company's future direction, which undermines the organizational stability that builds trust. No evidence of employee empowerment programs or cultural practices that create psychological safety.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): CEO Thomson's competitive framing — that News Corp succeeded 'while other media companies have floundered' — is classic finite-game language focused on rivals' failures rather than self-improvement [3]. The competitive posture emphasizes winning relative to peers rather than using competitive pressure to improve. No evidence of acknowledging rivals' strengths or using competitive dynamics as motivation for self-improvement.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): News Corp's transformation from a print-first media company to 61% digital revenue represents meaningful strategic evolution [1]. The company has selectively divested legacy assets (Foxtel stake), grown digital platforms (REA Group, Dow Jones digital), and entered new revenue streams (AI content licensing). However, the core business model remains media content creation and distribution — the company has evolved HOW it delivers content rather than fundamentally reinventing WHAT it does. The Dow Jones segment's achievement of 30% profit margins reflects operational excellence rather than existential flexibility [2].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): The decision to proactively license content to AI companies — rather than solely fight the technology — demonstrates willingness to adapt strategically when many media peers chose defensive litigation [3]. The divestiture of underperforming assets to focus on digital growth engines shows capital allocation discipline. However, News Corp has not demonstrated the pattern of repeatedly costly long-term bets that characterizes a 2/2. The digital transformation was driven by market necessity (print revenue decline) rather than proactive sacrifice of a profitable business in service of a cause.

investment_thesis: News Corp at 21.42x forward earnings offers a diversified media portfolio with accelerating digital transformation — 61% of FY2026 revenue is now digital, with full-year revenue of $9.03B (+7% YoY), net income of $743M (+15%), and operating cash flow of $1.24B (+26%) [1]. The crown jewels are Dow Jones (30% profit margins, premium WSJ brand) and REA Group (dominant Australian digital real estate, 19% Q4 revenue growth), which together provide a growth-and-moat combination rare in legacy media [2]. The proactive AI content licensing strategy monetizes News Corp's vast content archive rather than merely defending against disruption, and the conservative balance sheet (D/E 31.56%) provides financial flexibility for opportunistic acquisitions or capital returns. The Q4 FY2026 revenue growth of 11% — the fastest quarterly growth in four years — suggests accelerating momentum across all five segments.
thesis_continued: The bear case centers on structural media headwinds, low margins, and governance risk. Profit margin of 6.35% and ROE of 7.98% are well below quality thresholds, reflecting the capital-intensive legacy media operations that continue to drag on the higher-margin digital businesses [5]. The PEG ratio of 2.95 (near the 3.0 floor) indicates the market views the current growth rate as insufficient to justify the valuation. AI poses existential risk to the News Media segment — as AI-generated content improves and search referral traffic declines, traditional journalism advertising and subscription revenue face secular pressure that content licensing cannot fully offset [3]. The Murdoch family dual-class share structure concentrates control and has created governance instability (2024 succession dispute), limiting minority shareholder influence over strategic decisions. Estimated 5-year revenue CAGR of only ~3% reflects the structural challenges in growing legacy media assets. The Inspire Impact Score of 0 (MIXED) with no attributions in either direction suggests limited ESG differentiation for values-based investors.
key_catalysts: Dow Jones digital subscription and professional information services growth driving segment EBITDA margins to 30%+, with potential for the segment to re-rate as a standalone data/analytics business rather than a newspaper company [2]

REA Group international expansion and Move/Realtor.com recovery driving Digital Real Estate Services revenue growth of 19% in Q4 FY2026, with the Australian real estate market cyclical recovery providing multi-quarter tailwinds [1]

AI content licensing agreements with major technology platforms creating a new recurring revenue stream that monetizes News Corp's decades of proprietary content, with potential for expanded deal volume as AI training data demand accelerates [1][3]
key_risks: AI-driven disruption of traditional journalism — AI-generated content, declining search referral traffic, and audience migration to AI-powered information tools threaten the News Media segment's advertising and subscription revenue model, with content licensing unlikely to fully offset the structural decline [3]

Murdoch family dual-class share structure concentrates voting control and creates governance risk — the 2024 succession dispute highlighted family instability, and minority shareholders have no meaningful influence over strategic direction, CEO selection, or capital allocation [4]

Profit margin of 6.35% and ROE of 7.98% reflect structural capital inefficiency in legacy media operations, with no clear path to the 20%+ margins that would justify the current 21.42x forward P/E multiple [5]
